fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area; Detached Structure; Patio Area; Perimeter Fencing; Dense Vegetation; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Side Access; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Clear a path along at least one side of the main residence wide enough for responders to move on foot between the front and rear of the property.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure so responders can work along exterior walls.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing accessible from the street to provide a secondary foot-entry point if the driveway is blocked.
• Mark the detached structure with a visible label or number so responders arriving on scene can distinguish it from the main residence.
• Keep the patio area clear of stored items so responders can use it as a staging or treatment area.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure so responders can move directly between the two buildings.
• Post the property address visibly at the single driveway entrance so it is readable from both directions of travel.

wildfire.conditions: Large Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Between Structures
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches on large trees that hang directly over or within a few feet of the structure's roof and walls.
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structure to create more space between individual tree crowns.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the structure's foundation or walls.
• Clear dry leaves, needles, and small debris that collect against the structure from nearby trees.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their canopies do not touch or overlap each other.
• Remove or cut back vegetation growing between the structures to open up the space between them.
• Keep the ground beneath large trees near the structure clear of dead branches, leaves, and woody debris.
• Trim the lower branches of large trees near the structure up from the ground to reduce the chance of fire climbing into the canopy.
• Separate shrubs scattered across the open terrain near the structure so they do not form continuous patches leading toward the building.
